title: Mapping URLs to requests for modules and subresources generally

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
The motivation of https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/ was to have safeguards for third-party scripts and style sheets, but with the introduction of module scripts (and also the existence of `@import` and now `import()`) you have to make a choice between safeguarding and modern practices. This is also true for referrer policy, controlling credentials, and other things part of requests.

Furthermore, if you take a slightly broader view and include audio, fonts, images, video, and other subresources into your threat model, there are many places in the platform where you cannot safeguard as they only take a URL (e.g., `background-image`, `srcset`).

There's two classes of solutions that come up:

1. Update all places that only take a URL to also accept parameters in some way. It seems ever less likely that this will happen and it's not even desirable as a) some syntax would get rather complex for sometimes niche use cases and b) integrity invalidation when a nested resource updates would be bad.
2. Have a manifest that's available before the "preload scanner" sees URLs so it knows how to parse them. This could be declarative or imperative (though see https://github.com/WICG/import-maps/issues/70).

In #2640 we discussed some issues with the imperative variant of 2, but with a declarative version you should be able to get the final URL (well request) at URL parse time which would allow it to work well with the existing APIs. (Another way might be to require `import:` URLs to be used or some such if you want to go through the manifest, but avoiding special URLs seems nicer.)
